risks.note: The Company states that sugar price risk and supply chain disruptions are among its important market risks and that it is exposed to the usual price risk associated with fluctuation in sugar prices. Total exposure of the Company to commodities was disclosed at Rs 110,810 Mn, with material exposures to raw sugar and white sugar; the Company manages this through a Commodity Risk Management Policy and hedging in the international market.
risks.risk: Sugar price risk and commodity exposure

risks.note: Supply chain risks are stated to be mitigated by diversifying the supplier base to reduce dependence. The Indian outlook is described as remaining sensitive to monsoon trends, cane availability and recovery levels; erratic rainfall and lower sugar recovery in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka reduced production during the latter half of Sugar Season 2025-26.
risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and cane availability

risks.note: The business is described as commodity-linked and policy-sensitive. Ethanol offtake depends on the Government's Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme and on OMC procurement prices, which remained unchanged during the year, while domestic sugar realisations sit within a regulated minimum-selling-price framework the Government indicated will remain unchanged. Export and ethanol policy are named as factors the India outlook remains sensitive to.
risks.risk: Policy and regulatory dependence on ethanol and sugar pricing regimes

risks.note: The national ethanol feedstock mix has shifted materially, with grain-based ethanol accounting for 72% of supply against an original programme design that envisaged sugar-based ethanol contributing 55%, structurally reducing the share of the programme available to cane-based distillers.
risks.risk: Feedstock allocation shifting away from sugar-based ethanol

risks.note: White sugar premiums declined from USD 121/MT in the first quarter to USD 93/MT in the final quarter, reducing refinery margins and placing pressure on export-oriented refiners. Global refined sugar production forecast at 182.0 million MT creates a supply surplus, and refining spreads are named among the factors the India outlook remains sensitive to.
risks.risk: Compression of refining spreads and export margin exposure

risks.note: Export revenue dominates the revenue mix relative to domestic sales, and the forward order book is anchored on a small number of large relationships, notably the Coca-Cola global sugar contract for 175,000 MT during 2026 and 2027, alongside markets in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Africa and Somalia.

India's refining sector saw both expansion and rationalisation during the year: Shri Dutt increased capacity from 1,000 MT/day to 2,500 MT/day and two new refineries at Kandla are under development, only partially offset by EID Parry's closure of its 2,500 MT/day Kakinada refinery.
risks.risk: Competitive capacity additions in Indian sugar refining

risks.note: The Statutory Auditors reported observations on the audit trail (edit log) functionality in certain accounting software and on the post-facto ratification of a limited number of related party transactions; the Secretarial Auditors flagged delays in filing intimations/announcements with the Stock Exchanges under Regulation 30. The Corporate Governance Report also discloses penalty orders received from State Excise Parbhani, CGST & Central Excise Belagavi, the Income Tax Department and State Tax Gandhidham. The Board states corrective and preventive measures have been implemented.

currentContext.expansion: The Company operates six sugar mills (Munoli, Athani, Havalga, Pathri, Panchaganga and Raibag), two subsidiary sugar mills (Kolavi under Gokak Sugars Ltd. and Bulandshahr under Anamika Sugar Mills Pvt. Ltd.), two port-based refineries at Kandla and Haldia, three distilleries (Munoli, Athani and Havalga) and nine power plants including two of subsidiaries, with the Ajinkyatara co-generation unit held on a BOOT basis. Its build-out has been sequential rather than announced forward: a co-generation plant and 60 KLPD distillery at Munoli in 2000, a greenfield sugar mill at Athani in 2006, the 3,000 TPD port-based Kandla refinery in 2008, the 1,500 TPD Haldia refinery in 2011, the increase in Anamika Sugar Mills' capacity to 6,000 TCD in 2021, and the expansion of ethanol capacity from 720 KLPD to 1,250 KLPD in 2023 alongside the acquisition of Anamika Sugar Mills. Present installed capacity stands at 37,500 TCD of crushing, 1,250 KLPD of ethanol production, 5,500 TCD of raw sugar melting and 259 MW of co-generation. The Annual Report announces no new greenfield or brownfield project with a commissioning or ramp timeline; the forward initiative disclosed is commercial rather than capital — a five-year supply, marketing and distribution arrangement with AWL Agri Business Ltd. for the Madhur brand effective 1st July 2026, characterised as a royalty-led asset-light model under which the Company retains the Madhur trademark. Capacity change in the wider industry is noted as context only: Shri Dutt increased refining capacity from 1,000 MT/day to 2,500 MT/day, two new refineries at Kandla are under development, and EID Parry announced the closure of its 2,500 MT/day Kakinada refinery.

The Indian outlook is described as remaining sensitive to monsoon trends, cane availability and recovery levels; erratic rainfall and lower sugar recovery in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka reduced production during the latter half of Sugar Season 2025-26.
- The business is described as commodity-linked and policy-sensitive. Ethanol offtake depends on the Government's Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme and on OMC procurement prices, which remained unchanged during the year, while domestic sugar realisations sit within a regulated minimum-selling-price framework the Government indicated will remain unchanged. Export and ethanol policy are named as factors the India outlook remains sensitive to.
- The national ethanol feedstock mix has shifted materially, with grain-based ethanol accounting for 72% of supply against an original programme design that envisaged sugar-based ethanol contributing 55%, structurally reducing the share of the programme available to cane-based distillers.
- White sugar premiums declined from USD 121/MT in the first quarter to USD 93/MT in the final quarter, reducing refinery margins and placing pressure on export-oriented refiners. Global refined sugar production forecast at 182.0 million MT creates a supply surplus, and refining spreads are named among the factors the India outlook remains sensitive to.
- Export revenue dominates the revenue mix relative to domestic sales, and the forward order book is anchored on a small number of large relationships, notably the Coca-Cola global sugar contract for 175,000 MT during 2026 and 2027, alongside markets in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Africa and Somalia.
- India's refining sector saw both expansion and rationalisation during the year: Shri Dutt increased capacity from 1,000 MT/day to 2,500 MT/day and two new refineries at Kandla are under development, only partially offset by EID Parry's closure of its 2,500 MT/day Kakinada refinery.
- The Statutory Auditors reported observations on the audit trail (edit log) functionality in certain accounting software and on the post-facto ratification of a limited number of related party transactions; the Secretarial Auditors flagged delays in filing intimations/announcements with the Stock Exchanges under Regulation 30. The Corporate Governance Report also discloses penalty orders received from State Excise Parbhani, CGST & Central Excise Belagavi, the Income Tax Department and State Tax Gandhidham. The Board states corrective and preventive measures have been implemented.
